about:
Cirtronics Corporation, a contract manufacturer based in Milford, New Hampshire, was founded in 1979 by Gerardine Ferlins. Ferlins aimed to build a company that valued people as much as profits, extending that focus to customers, community, and suppliers. The company operates under an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), making every employee a part-owner.

The company provides end-to-end manufacturing services for complex electromechanical systems, including engineering support, supply chain management, production, testing, logistics, and repair and refurbishment. Its capabilities span full system integration, complex sub-assemblies, and board-level assembly. Cirtronics emphasizes lean manufacturing practices, with green belts on staff, and uses an integrated IT platform to deliver real-time production information and work instructions.

Cirtronics serves the robotics, medical and life sciences, defense and security, and industrial markets. Its customer base includes Ava Robotics, Image Stream Medical, Doble Engineering, Heller Industries, Rapiscan Systems, and Belmont Medical Technologies. The company also operates as a repair depot and refurbishment center, housing spares and providing upgrades for deployed products.

Cirtronics differentiates itself through its employee-ownership culture, which it says aligns the interests of customers and staff, fostering better communication and dedicated teamwork. The company's "Precision Engagement" approach tailors manufacturing programs to each client, and its quality management system monitors key processes with statistical process control. A focus on design for manufacturability and supplier qualification aims to reduce total cost of ownership.
